parts.text: Which claim about this arrangement is correct?

options.text: The Moon is toward the Sun, so little or none of its illuminated half faces Earth.
The Moon is nearly opposite the Sun, so the full illuminated half faces Earth.
Earth lies between the Sun and the Moon, producing a bright full circle.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: The diagram shows the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon on a day when Nikhil sees almost no bright part of the Moon from Earth.

part_answers.answer: When the Moon is toward the Sun, the illuminated half faces away from Earth, so almost no bright part is seen (new Moon).

teacher.key_rationale: New Moon occurs when the Moon is toward the Sun, so little of the illuminated half faces Earth. Opposite the Sun is full Moon, not this case.
teacher.figure_note: Sun, Earth, Moon with Moon toward the Sun (new Moon).
